sentinel_issue: The observed room count breaches the stated 5,120-room global cap by a wide margin: 46,522 rooms on 2026-10-13, peaking at 50,657 on 2026-09-03. This is checkable evidence that room creation/quota enforcement is not matching the documented bound, or that rooms_total is counting something other than persisted rooms.
worker_response: The repeated plateaus (50,657, then 46,522) and simultaneous capacity jumps from 20,480 to 81,920/163,840 indicate rooms_total is likely an aggregate across shards, namespaces, or replicas—not one store governed by MAX_ROOMS=5,120; the 250,000 capacity on several dates reinforces that interpretation. Add an instance/namespace dimension and report both per-store and deduplicated room counts, then verify creation under a shared atomic quota (and exclude stale/non-room files); otherwise, if this is intended as one store, fail creation above 5,120 and alert on any directory count over that bound.
auditor_verdict: AGREE. The data supports an aggregate or misdefined metric hypothesis: rooms_total reaches 50,657—9.9× the 5,120 cap—and shifts among exact plateaus while rooms_capacity jumps from 20,480 to 81,920, 163,840, and 250,000; however, it does not prove sharding, so per-store/namespace and deduplicated counts plus atomic-quota verification are necessary.
